reader.requirement: After an unsuccessful I-O operation (not covered by an AT END phrase) the compiler must run exactly one USE procedure: the one naming the file explicitly if any, otherwise the INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND procedure matching the mode the file is open in or is being opened in, excluding files named explicitly in another USE for the same condition.

Grep of src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO for the same: FileConnector.Edition feeds sharing, CLOSE LOCK, relative/indexed status choices, none on the declarative selection path (OpenModeView, the file-name/mode switch). The selection tiers are edition-invariant by a recorded determination on UseTierEmitter (kb/Work PB344).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers INPUT and OUTPUT tiers only (indexed READ 47/10/46 and a failed OPEN INPUT); the explicit file-name tier, its exclusion from the mode tiers, I-O, EXTEND, failed OPEN I-O/EXTEND and the AT END precedence are not exercised

probes.printed: T1 READ on OUTPUT file: DECL-OUT 47; T2 FA (explicit USE) at end, no phrase: DECL-FA 10 (not DECL-IN); T3 AT END phrase: 'T3 AT END 10', no declarative; T4 READ after at end: DECL-IN 46; T5 REWRITE without READ in I-O: DECL-IO 43; T6 READ on EXTEND file: DECL-EX 47; T7/T8/T9 failed OPEN INPUT/I-O/EXTEND of an absent file: DECL-IN/DECL-IO/DECL-EX with 35; T10 CLOSE of a file not open: 42, no declarative; T11 FA open OUTPUT, READ: DECL-FA 47 (not DECL-OUT); control returns to the next statement each time
probes.expected: GR5 a)-e): file-name procedure for FA; mode procedure by open or being-opened mode for others, excluding FA; AT END phrase takes precedence; GR6 return to next statement

probes.printed: USE ... ON EXTEND (the 1985 level-2 boxed item e) compiles and runs at --std 85 (DECL-EX lines above)
probes.expected: GR5 e) EXTEND procedure for a file open or being opened in extend mode

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR5  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: All five lettered items and the AT END precedence behave as the 1985 text says at --std 85 on sequential files; the witness adds indexed coverage. The selection is generated once by UseTierEmitter and consults no edition.

refuter.evidence: ruse1-002 (--std 85): USE ON FA FB (multi-name list, second name) at end -> DECL-AB 10 only; READ AT END then READ AT END at status 46 -> AT END phrase skipped, DECL-IN 46 (phrase takes precedence only for at-end); failed OPEN OUTPUT to a missing directory -> DECL-OUT 30 (being-opened output tier, not exercised by reader); OPEN INPUT of a file open OUTPUT -> DECL-IN 41 (being-opened mode chosen; text lets both b and c read on it, a defensible choice); reopen I-O after close -> DECL-IO 10/46; READ/WRITE on never-opened or closed file -> 47/48 and no declarative (no mode applies). ruse2-002: nested program with USE ON FH and containing GLOBAL USE ON INPUT -> FG fails in inner: OUTER-GLOBAL-IN; FH: INNER-FH only. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR5 'in the process of being opened in the input mode'; OK §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1.
